classification.difficultyReason: Select two pairs of similar triangles in a parallelogram configuration and connect corresponding-side ratios with the given division of a side.

content.prompt: $ABCD$ is a parallelogram with $E$ on $BC$ such that $BE=2EC$. The line $AE$ and the line $DC$ intersect at $F$.

answer.worked:
$AB\parallel CF$, since opposite sides of a parallelogram are parallel. Thus $\angle EBA=\angle ECF$ (alternate angles). Also $\angle BEA=\angle CEF$ (vertically opposite angles). The remaining angles are equal, so $\triangle BEA\sim\triangle CEF$ (AAA).

$$\begin{align*}\frac{AB}{CF}&=\frac{BE}{CE}\\\frac{AB}{CF}&=2\\AB&=2CF.\end{align*}$$

$AD\parallel EC$, so $\angle ADF=\angle ECF$ (corresponding angles). Also $\angle AFD=\angle EFC$ (common angle at $F$). The remaining angles are equal, so $\triangle AFD\sim\triangle EFC$ (AAA).

Opposite sides of a parallelogram are equal:
$$\begin{align*}AD&=BC\\AD&=BE+EC\\AD&=2EC+EC\\AD&=3EC.\end{align*}$$
Matching sides therefore give
$$\begin{align*}\frac{AF}{EF}&=\frac{AD}{EC}\\\frac{AF}{EF}&=3\\AF&=3EF.\end{align*}$$
